faqs.a: Upload the photo and move the block-size slider. Bigger blocks mean stronger pixelation. Press Download to save the pixelated PNG or JPG.
faqs.q: How do I pixelate a photo?

faqs.a: Yes. Pixelation replaces whole blocks with their average color, permanently discarding the detail inside each block. It cannot be undone from the saved file.
faqs.q: Does pixelation really hide the details?

faqs.a: Use large blocks (32–64 px) for faces and text you must hide. Small blocks (4–10 px) only give a retro mosaic look and may still reveal shapes.
faqs.q: How strong should the pixelation be to hide a face?

faqs.a: The preview always shows the full-size output, so what you see is exactly what downloads, at the original resolution.
faqs.q: Is the preview the same quality as the download?

faqs.a: No. Everything happens on a canvas in your browser; your photo is never uploaded to any server.

pixelate-image.formula:
blocks_x = round(width / block_size)
blocks_y = round(height / block_size)
block_color(x, y) = average color of the block_size × block_size region
howTo: Upload the image you want to pixelate with the file picker.
Move the block-size slider: small values give a subtle mosaic, large values give heavy censor-style blocks.
Watch the live preview update as you drag.
Choose PNG or JPG output format.
Press Download to save the pixelated image.
keyFacts: Pixelation shrinks the image to a tiny grid, then scales it back up without smoothing.
Each block shows the average color of its region, which permanently removes fine detail.
Block sizes range from 2 px (subtle mosaic) to 64 px (heavy censor effect).
The block count readout tells you exactly how many blocks the image is reduced to.
The output keeps the original pixel dimensions.

limitations: Pixelation is destructive — the hidden detail cannot be recovered from the saved file.
Very small blocks may still reveal text or faces; use large blocks for real privacy.
The effect covers the whole image; selective-area pixelation is not included.
Animated GIFs are processed as a single still frame.

pixelate-image.workedExample:
An 800 × 600 px photo with a 20 px block size:
blocks_x = round(800 / 20) = 40
blocks_y = round(600 / 20) = 30
The image is reduced to a 40 × 30 grid (1,200 blocks) and scaled back up with hard edges. At 64 px blocks it becomes only 13 × 9 blocks — strong enough to hide any face.
